newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares gain 2.55 pct to new record.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares gain 2.55 pct to new record.

text.p: Istanbul shares leapt an average 2.55 percent on Tuesday, in continued selective activity after Monday's 1.47 percent down correction to the recent rally, brokers said.

The IMKB-100 .XU100 gained 29 points to close at a new all-time high of 1,165, compared to Friday's previous record of 1,153. In dollar terms, it was unchanged from Friday's record high $1.04, and firmed from Monday's $1.02.
Trade volume rose to 21.14 trillion lira from Monday's 14.48 trillion lira and neared Friday's 25.47 trillion.
Brokers said selective activity continued from the first session as players switched to cheaper shares from those with stronger premiums, with the help of rising liquidity.

The market index which hit a midday record of 1,168 at the end of the first session, had soared 18.1 percent, breaking record closes on seven consecutive days after the market reopened on January 2, following a five-day holiday.

Downward money and bond market rates fuelled by surplus cash, quiet trends in the currency market and 1996 profit prospects of companies were the main factors behind the uptrend since the beginning of 1997.

Of the 238 shares traded, gainers outdid losers sharply by 156 to 30 and 52 closed steady. The IMKB Industrial .XUSIN rose 2.25 percent to 1,227, the IMKB Services .XUHIZ jumped 3.35 percent to 1,204 and the IMKB Finacial .XUMAL leapt 2.66 percent to 1,119.
Leading actives were utilities Aktas Elektrik, up 5,000 lira at 120,000 and Cukurova Elektrik, up 5,000 lira at 150,000. They they made up 8.4 percent of the total turnover.
